svg.title: Colocated MoE, synchronous AFD, and asynchronous AFD timing comparison
svg.desc: Three timing panels on a shared time scale. The first shows two colocated MoE layers with global synchronization bubbles. The second shows synchronous AFD with two stages and waiting after both Attention stages have been sent. The third shows asynchronous AFD consuming complete DP-stage work items after their sends finish.
svg.text: Attention imbalance becomes a global MoE synchronization bubble.
No microbatching: every layer waits for the slowest Attention DP before MoE can advance.
The dual-stage panels below split—not shorten—the same Attention work: full batch = S0 + S1.
Dual-stage execution overlaps remote FFN work, but FFN receive still waits for every DP in each stage.
The first exposed Attention idle appears only after both stage sends.
Each DP sends independently; FFN compute starts only after its synchronous receive has collected every DP contribution.
Each complete DP-stage work item is consumed independently in readiness order.
Dual-stage execution hides local FFN latency; asynchronous AFD additionally removes cross-DP rendezvous bubbles.
